title: DSU / Union-Find & MST (Kruskal, Prim)
relevance: High — connectivity, cycle detection, “min cost to connect”, and offline merge queries dominate OAs; Kruskal+DSU is the standard MST interview package.
company_notes: Provinces / friend circles / accounts: merge entities sharing a key (city, email, language) and count groups or sizes (LC 547 / 721, CF News Distribution). Cables & redundancy: min ops to connect all computers or which edge creates a cycle (LC 1319 / 684) — Amazon/Meta-style graph OAs. Min cost to wire sites: Manhattan points or city roads → MST (LC 1584, CSES Road Reparation); sometimes power-station OR wire → virtual node. Equality constraints: union on a==b then validate a!=b (LC 990); same pattern as same-gang / opposite-gang 2-SAT-lite with DSU.

phases.goal: Map the prompt to DSU connectivity, cycle/redundant edges, MST wiring, or offline merge tricks from signal wording.

must_hit.point: Signal words like provinces/friends/network, redundant cable, connect all cities, max edge on path ≤ X, or repair roads with min cost point to DSU and/or MST.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names those signal phrases and ties them to disjoint-set merges or spanning-tree cost.

must_hit.point: Use DSU when edges arrive over time, you need component sizes/counts, or you must detect a cycle while adding edges.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says incremental edges / component bookkeeping / failed merge = cycle.

must_hit.point: Kruskal is sort edges by weight then add if endpoints differ (DSU); Prim grows one tree with a priority queue.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts sorted-edge Kruskal+DSU with PQ tree-growth Prim.

must_hit.point: Offline tricks include processing edges light→heavy or reversing deletions as unions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions light-to-heavy offline merges or reverse-time unions for deletions/bridge collapse.

probes: What wording makes this DSU connectivity, a redundant/cycle edge, MST wiring, or an offline reverse-merge problem?
Would you reach for Kruskal+DSU or Prim here, and why?

hints.1: Look for shared keys, connect-all / min-cost wiring, or edges added/deleted over time.
hints.2: Shared key / group sizes → DSU; failed merge → cycle; sort+union → Kruskal; dense/implicit points → Prim; deletions → reverse unions.
hints.3: Say: provinces/friends/redundant cable/connect cities/repair roads → DSU/MST; edges over time, sizes/counts, or cycle-while-adding → DSU; Kruskal = sort by weight add if endpoints differ; Prim = PQ grow; offline light→heavy or reverse deletions as unions.

phases.goal: State the DSU merge rule, Kruskal/Prim MST plan, and any reverse or offline-by-weight strategy before coding.

must_hit.point: Maintain disjoint sets so same-component queries and merges stay nearly O(1) amortized with path compression plus union by size/rank.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names path compression and union by size/rank for nearly O(1) amortized merges/finds.

must_hit.point: Kruskal: sort edges ascending, add iff union succeeds, stop at n-1 edges, and detect if the graph stays disconnected.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes sort → successful unions only → n-1 edges or IMPOSSIBLE/disconnected.

must_hit.point: Prim: binary-heap grow from a source; prefer when E ≈ V^2 or distances are implicit (points).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says heap Prim from a source for dense or implicit complete graphs like Manhattan points.

must_hit.point: Reverse technique: treat deletions or bridges-collapse by processing reverse as unions (Decayed Bridges / Destroying Array).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Flips delete→add and unions in reverse time, tracking sizes or sums.

must_hit.point: Offline by weight: sort edges and queries together and maintain binom(sz,2)-style pair counts as components merge (Path Queries).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sorts edges+queries by weight and updates pairs-in-component while merging.

probes: Walk through Kruskal versus Prim for this graph—when is each preferable?
If edges are deleted over time or queries are offline by weight, how do you rewrite the problem as unions?

hints.1: Separate live same-component merges from MST construction and from reverse/offline rewrites.
hints.2: Kruskal = sort + union until n-1; Prim = heap grow when dense/implicit; deletions → reverse unions; weight queries → sort edges+queries.
hints.3: Say: path compression + union by size/rank; Kruskal sort ascending, union succeeds, stop at n-1, detect disconnected; Prim binary-heap when E ≈ V^2 or implicit points; reverse deletions as unions; offline sort edges+queries and track pair counts on merges.

phases.goal: Code the DSU template, component bookkeeping, Kruskal/Prim mechanics, and cycle/redundant-edge detection from memory.

must_hit.point: DSU template: parent, size/rank, recursive find with path compression, union by size/rank returning bool.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches parent + size/rank arrays, compressing find, and bool-returning union.

must_hit.point: Component bookkeeping on roots: count of components, size of each root, optional sum/xor/min on the root.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Tracks component count and per-root size (and optional aggregates) as unions succeed.

must_hit.point: Cycle / redundant edge: a failed union means the edge closes a cycle (first failed union is the answer on Redundant Connection).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says union returns false ⇒ redundant cycle edge.

must_hit.point: Network connect: need components-1 moves iff there are enough redundant edges.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States answer components-1 only when spare same-component edges suffice.

must_hit.point: Equality equations: union on == first, then validate !=; accounts merge maps email→id, unions, then groups.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Processes equalities before inequalities, or email→id union then group by root.

probes: Write find/union from memory—what does a false union return mean?
How do you bookkeep component sizes, and how do you handle == then != equations?

hints.1: Start from parent/size arrays and what union’s boolean means.
hints.2: Path-compress find; union by size/rank; failed union = cycle; keep count/size on roots; equalities before inequalities.
hints.3: Say: parent + size/rank, recursive find with path compression, union by size/rank returns bool; track component count/size (optional sum/xor/min); false union = cycle/redundant; components-1 moves iff enough redundants; == unions then check !=; email→id union then group.

phases.goal: State DSU’s amortized cost and when Prim’s dense/implicit setting beats Kruskal.

must_hit.point: With path compression and union by size/rank, find/union are nearly O(1) amortized.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites nearly O(1) amortized under those two optimizations.

must_hit.point: Prefer Prim’s binary-heap grow when E ≈ V^2 or distances are implicit (points), where materializing every edge for Kruskal is awkward.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Chooses Prim for dense or implicit complete graphs like Manhattan points.

must_hit.point: Kruskal still needs a spanning tree of n-1 edges; fewer successful unions means the graph is disconnected.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties finishing with fewer than n-1 tree edges to disconnected / IMPOSSIBLE.

probes: What is the amortized cost of find/union with path compression and union by size/rank?
When do you prefer Prim over Kruskal for points or dense graphs?

hints.1: Name the two DSU optimizations and the dense/implicit Prim cue.
hints.2: Path compression + union by size/rank → nearly O(1); Prim when E ≈ V^2 or implicit distances; Kruskal needs n-1 edges.
hints.3: Say: nearly O(1) amortized with path compression + union by size/rank; Prim binary-heap when E ≈ V^2 or implicit points; Kruskal stops at n-1 edges or reports disconnected.

phases.goal: Catch reverse-time mistakes, equality order bugs, disconnected MST, and missed virtual-node / dual-forest variants.

must_hit.point: Processing deletions forward instead of reverse-as-unions breaks Decayed Bridges / Destroying Array–style asks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists delete→add reverse unions, e.g. inconvenient pairs via n(n-1)/2 minus size products.

must_hit.point: Validating != before unioning all == (or skipping the empty-language edge case) wrong-answers equality / shared-key DSU.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Does all == merges first, then checks !=; mentions empty shared-key cases when relevant.

must_hit.point: Reporting an MST cost without detecting disconnection (Road Reparation → IMPOSSIBLE) or without enough spare edges for components-1 reconnects.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Checks spanning connectivity / IMPOSSIBLE and spare-edge budget before components-1.

must_hit.point: Missing MST variants: virtual node for build-facility-or-connect (Shichikuji), dual DSU forests that both stay acyclic, or bit-greedy connectivity checks (MinOr).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names virtual node 0, dual-forest edge adds, or drop high OR-bits while DSU stays connected.

probes: What goes wrong if you process bridge deletions in forward time?
How do you order == vs !=, and when is the MST answer IMPOSSIBLE?

hints.1: Check time direction, equality order, and whether the forest actually spans.
hints.2: Deletions → reverse unions; == before !=; need n-1 tree edges or IMPOSSIBLE; spare edges for components-1; watch virtual-node / dual-DSU variants.
hints.3: Say: reverse deletions as unions (n(n-1)/2 minus size products); equalities first then !=; disconnected Kruskal → IMPOSSIBLE; components-1 iff enough redundants; virtual node / dual forests / bit-greedy DSU checks for variants.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Kruskal sorts edges by weight and adds iff endpoints differ (DSU), stopping at n-1 edges; Prim grows one tree with a binary-heap priority queue and is preferable when E ≈ V^2 or distances are implicit (e.g. Manhattan complete graphs, where Prim is often cleaner).
Both can count components or take a min per component (Rumor); prefer DSU when edges arrive over time, you need incremental sizes after each union, or you must detect cycles while adding edges.

tradeoffs.topic: Online unions vs offline light→heavy / reverse deletions
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Live unions answer same-component and size queries as edges appear; when queries are by max edge weight or the timeline is deletions/bridge collapse, rewrite offline—sort edges light→heavy with queries, or process reverse time as unions.

tradeoffs.topic: Plain MST vs virtual-node / bit-greedy MST
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Plain Kruskal/Prim wires sites with edge costs only; “build a facility or connect” adds a virtual node (station cost = edge to node 0); MinOr-style asks drop high OR-bits while DSU confirms the graph stays connected.

gotchas.trap: Treating every edge as tree-worthy without checking union’s return value.
gotchas.correction: A failed union means the edge closes a cycle; on Redundant Connection the first failed union is the answer.

gotchas.trap: Answering reconnect cost as components-1 without checking spare edges.
gotchas.correction: You need components-1 moves iff there are enough redundant (same-component) edges.

gotchas.trap: Checking != constraints before unioning all == equalities.
gotchas.correction: Process a==b unions first, then validate a!=b (LC 990).

gotchas.trap: Processing deletions or decaying bridges in forward chronological order.
gotchas.correction: Reverse the timeline and treat additions as unions; Decayed Bridges uses inconvenient pairs = n(n-1)/2 minus size products on merges.

gotchas.trap: Printing an MST total when fewer than n-1 edges were successfully united.
gotchas.correction: Detect disconnection and output IMPOSSIBLE (Road Reparation) instead of a partial cost.

gotchas.trap: Modeling “build power station or wire to another city” with only city–city edges.
gotchas.correction: Add a virtual node (station cost = edge to node 0) and run MST, then reconstruct edges.
